title: Grand Theft Auto: the evolution of a controversial franchise
summary: MANILA, Philippines – This month of November, Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI, one of the most highly anticipated games will finally be released on PC and modern consoles after over a decade of teases,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – This month of November, Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI, one of the most highly anticipated games will finally be released on PC and modern consoles after over a decade of teases, delays, and outright controversy.

As the eighth mainline entry in Rockstar Games’ action-adventure open world video game series, GTA VI is the latest in a long line of games where players can basically do anything in an open-world, sandbox style world.
Each game follows storylines set in fictional cities based on real-life locations, where players take control of different protagonists who are typically criminals with their own respective agendas.
Early beginnings
Before it became the multi-billion dollar franchise it is today, Grand Theft Auto’s humble beginnings began with its namesake title in 1997.

blocks.caption: Grand Theft Auto box cover. Image via Rockstar Games

blocks.text: Released for the MS-DOS and Windows and ported to the PlayStation, the first GTA was a top-down view game that introduced players to the three main cities that would be prominently featured throughout the series: Liberty City, Vice City, and San Andreas.
Each location is inspired by a real-life American city, with players choosing and guiding a character as they complete missions in order to rise through the criminal underworld and retire in peace.
GTA’s two-dimensional era would continue with a sequel in Grand Theft Auto 2 released in 1999.

Unlike its predecessor and later games, it would be set in a retrofuturistic location known as “Anywhere City” and introduce new elements such as a save system and earning respect with syndicates by successfully completing jobs.
GTA 2 would also be the first game to be published by Rockstar Games – who took over publishing duties from BMG Interactive and have been the custodians of the series ever since.

The rise of open-world and 3D
By 2001, three-dimensional gaming was in full swing and the next generation of gaming consoles were led by Sony’s highly successful PlayStation 2.
Grand Theft Auto III was released in October that year, and revolutionized the way open-world, sandbox style games were presented in video games.

blocks.caption: Grand Theft Auto III: The Definitive Edition launched in 2021. Image via Rockstar Games

blocks.text: Pushing the boundaries of violence and sexual content like no other, GTA III helped usher in the 3D universe of games and is considered a landmark title in the history of gaming – selling over 14.5 million copies worldwide.
By the following year in 2002, Rockstar Games took a bigger swing at things by releasing their fourth mainline entry in the series with Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.

Doubling down on nostalgia and placing the setting of the game in 1986, players took control of the first speaking protagonist of the series in Tommy Vercetti – an Italian-American gangster who is sent to the fictional Vice City after serving a long prison sentence and fights his way to rise atop the city’s criminal underworld.

Building on the foundations of the previous game, GTA Vice City introduced more innovations and conventions such as more cars, more modes of transportation such as boats and planes, and a lot of references to the 1980’s – specifically the films and shows that left an indelible mark in that era of popular culture.

The game also featured a wider selection of music and iconic tracks that made up its awesome soundtrack – which would become a signature element of future games as popular musicians and labels would license their music to be part of the growing GTA franchise.
Wrapping up the 3D universe trilogy of games would be 2004’s Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, which would add even more features to the series that would propel it forward as an open-world game.

With new improvements such as the ability to swim (which was a death sentence in previous games) and the inclusion of RPG elements that added layers of customization to the game, players could change the main character’s stats as well as their overall appearance (including muscle mass and size).
Set in the 1990’s, players took control of Carl “CJ’ Johnson, an African-American gangster who returns to help his family in a time of crisis.

Along with even more pop culture references and music, San Andreas would be the most expansive entry at the time as it was the first GTA title to incorporate one huge island consisting of three different locations to explore in Los Santos, San Fierro, and Las Venturas.

Following Vice City and San Andreas success, Rockstar Games would release a number of spin-off entries that would help the Grand Theft Auto universe expand beyond console and PC platforms, with games such as GTA: Advance, GTA: Liberty City Stories, GTA: Vice City Stories, and GTA: China Town Wars hitting portable handheld devices such as the Gameboy Advance, Nintendo 3DS, and PlayStation Portable.

These games would feature their own unique set of protagonists and help expand the stories of the main GTA titles, with Vice City Stories for example set a few years before GTA: Vice City and putting players in control of Victor Vance – the brother of Tommy Vercetti’s one time ally and friend, Lance Vance.
Going high-definition
When the seventh generation of video game consoles arrived with the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360, all eyes were towards Rockstar Games’ next entry in the GTA franchise.

Enter Grand Theft Auto IV in 2008: which brought players back to Liberty City and centered around the adventures of Eastern European immigrant Niko Bellic as he tries to make a new life while escaping from his past as a war veteran.

The game would receive critical acclaim and would introduce the HD universe to the GTA saga. GTA IV would also be supplemented by two episodic expansion packs that featured new protagonists and interconnected storyline – The Lost and the Damned and The Ballad of Gay Tony.

As the dawn of the eight generation of video game platforms arrived in 2013, Rockstar Games had one last ace up their sleeve to bid farewell to the PS3 and Xbox 360 by releasing Grand Theft Auto V: their most ambitious and bold entry in the GTA series yet.

Taking players back to a highly detailed and expansive Los Santos, the new sequel puts players in control of three protagonists – Michael De Santa, Franklin Clinton, and Trevor Philips, as they navigate through a sea of criminals, heists, and government agency corruption in order to stay alive.
The game is the first to introduce its multiplayer online component in Grand Theft Auto Online, allowing 30 players to interact and play with each other in a variety of game modes set in Los Santos.

blocks.caption: Grand Theft Auto V poster. Image via Rockstar Games

blocks.text: GTA V proved to be a critical and financial success, and was the first game in the series to earn one billion dollars in the first three days of its release. It would get multiple rereleases in succeeding console generations, with upscaled graphics, performance, and improvements given to the game when it was rereleased for the PS4, Xbox One, PS5, and Xbox Series X.
The future awaits

Now as we welcome the release of the long awaited Grand Theft Auto VI, what quality of life additions and gameplay changes can we expect Rockstar Games to add in its eighth mainline entry in the franchise?

Only time will tell for sure, but it’s almost certainly a guarantee that this game will break records and sell billions as fans prepare to return to Vice City and explore the fictional state of Leonida while following the exploits of its new criminal duo leads in Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos.
Grand Theft Auto VI will be released digitally for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S on November 19.
